title: Pukekohe Indian Association Marks 90 Years With Diwali-Halloween Celebration
excerpt: The Pukekohe Indian Association and Franklin Indian Cultural Club host a free Diwali celebration at the PIA Event Centre on Saturday, October 31, from 5pm to 9pm - with dance, a fashion show, fireworks and Halloween costumes welcome.
body:
• Pukekohe's annual Diwali celebration is extra special this year: the Pukekohe Indian Association (PIA) marks its 90th anniversary, presenting the event with the Franklin Indian Cultural Club (FICC).
  • The reader's plan: the free celebration runs on Saturday, October 31, from 5pm to 9pm at the PIA Event Centre on Ward Street, Pukekohe - and Halloween costumes are welcome, with lollies for those who dress up.
  • Organisers expect between 300 and 400 attendees, following a strong turnout last year, with children's rides, dance performances, a fashion show, stalls run by local businesses and fireworks.
  • The current annual event has run for less than a decade, but the PIA has celebrated Diwali in various forms throughout its 90-year history.

Pukekohe's annual Diwali celebration carries an extra weight this year. The Pukekohe Indian Association (PIA) is marking its 90th anniversary, and the festival of lights it presents with the Franklin Indian Cultural Club (FICC) has been built as an open invitation to the whole Franklin district, according to the Franklin Times.

The free event is set for Saturday, October 31, at the PIA Event Centre. Because the date doubles as Halloween, organisers are embracing both festivities rather than asking families to choose. "Come dressed up in Halloween costumes and grab some lollies!" PIA secretary and FICC founder Arshdeep Kaur confirms.

"It's not just important for the Indian community to celebrate, but it's also nice to showcase our culture in a positive manner, inviting others to 'our house' to become part of the celebration."

— Arshdeep Kaur, Secretary, Pukekohe Indian Association

An Association Rooted in Franklin's Market Gardens

The anniversary reaches back to one of New Zealand's oldest Indian community stories. An Indian community developed in Pukekohe during the 1930s and 1940s around the town's market gardens, and local Indians formed the Pukekohe Indian Association in that era. In 1953, the Nehru Hall was constructed in Pukekohe for the Indian committee - the first Indian community hall built in New Zealand. When that hall grew too small for large events such as weddings, the association opened the PIA Events Centre in 1999, the Ward Street venue that now hosts the Diwali celebration.

Kaur says the point of the anniversary event is how much Franklin itself has changed. "The community has grown so much, and the dynamics of Franklin have changed," she says. The event is an opportunity for Franklin's growing population - of all cultures and ethnicities - to get together.

What Is On at the PIA Event Centre

The festivities begin at 5pm on October 31 and run to 9pm, per the event's What's On listing, which confirms entry is free. The programme features children's rides, dance performances, a fashion show and stalls run by local businesses. Fireworks close the arc of the evening - they were a big hit when introduced to the event last year.

Following a strong turnout last year, Kaur expects between 300 and 400 attendees. "People love to come back year after year, especially the performers. We have a nice hall and stage that they love dancing on," she says. "But we also love to see more and more people [enjoying the occasion] and we reach out to the schools to see if their students and their families can come along as well."

A Diaspora Landmark, Shared With the Neighbours

For Indian families in Franklin and across the wider Auckland diaspora, the evening is both a festival and a statement of permanence: a community that built New Zealand's first Indian hall in 1953 is now inviting the district's newest arrivals - of every background - into its own hall to celebrate. Readers within reach of Pukekohe need no ticket and no invitation beyond the one Kaur has issued: arrive at the PIA Event Centre on Ward Street from 5pm on Saturday, October 31, in Diwali dress or Halloween costume, and join the celebration.
